HK: Global risk-on lifts, but weak-side peg drains liquidity.
Policy: Rate and reserve requirement cuts delivered, system liquidity still tight.

summary: Mainland stuck in stagflation with growth improving; Hong Kong buoyed by global risk-on but weakened by peg outflows.
regime_read: China remains in Stagflation, but the growth picture is improving quickly — the growth reading has rebounded from its recent trough. Inflation is steady and positive, not yet cooling. So the map still says stagnation with price pressures, but the engine is starting to turn. The dominant driver today is the gap between policy easing and actual system liquidity: the central bank has cut rates and reserve requirements, yet its own stance still reads neutral and the liquidity overlay points to contraction — the water has been released at the tap, but it has not yet reached the pipes. Hong Kong sits in Goldilocks on the map, fueled by a strong global risk appetite that is pushing up U.S. stocks and emerging markets. But the Hong Kong dollar is pinned to the weak side of its trading band, signaling capital outflows. That drainage of cash is the anchor holding back what would otherwise be a risk-on rally. The fear-and-greed gauge is in greed territory, suggesting the market is already priced for good news, leaving little room for surprises.
